title: High-Protein Cottage Cheese Cookie Dough
description: This high-protein cottage cheese cookie dough delivers 19g of protein in just 10 minutes of total prep. Blended cottage cheese creates a silky base mixed with oat flour and chocolate chips. Save this recipe for your next meal prep snack.
steps: Combine 1 cup low-fat cottage cheese (225 g), 2 tbsp pure maple syrup (30 ml), and 1 tsp vanilla extract (5 ml) in a high-speed blender.
Blend on high speed for 45 to 60 seconds until completely smooth and silky with no remaining curd lumps.
Scrape the blended liquid into a medium bowl, then add 2 scoops vanilla whey protein powder (60 g), 1 cup oat flour (90 g), and 1/4 tsp fine sea salt.

Stir with a silicone spatula for 1 to 2 minutes until a thick, cohesive dough forms with no visible dry streaks. If the dough is too stiff, fold in unsweetened almond milk (up to 2 tbsp / 30 ml), 1 tbsp at a time, until the desired texture is reached.
Fold in 1/3 cup mini dark chocolate chips (60 g) until evenly distributed.
Divide into 4 portion cups and serve immediately, or chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes until firm and scoopable.
tips: Use casein or a whey-casein blend for an even thicker, more realistic cookie dough texture.
Heat-treat the oat flour in the microwave for 30 seconds if you prefer a toasted flour flavor.
Adjust consistency by adding 1 extra tablespoon of almond milk if your protein powder is very absorbent.
storage: Store in sealed containers in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Freeze in small portions for up to 1 month.

video_script.hook: Make edible cookie dough with 19 grams of protein per serving.
steps_short: Blend cottage cheese, maple syrup, vanilla, and almond milk until smooth.
Pour into a bowl and add protein powder, oat flour, and salt.
Stir thoroughly until a thick cookie dough forms.
Fold in mini dark chocolate chips until evenly mixed.
Chill for 15 minutes to reach an ultra-scoopable texture.

issues: Step 1 unconditionally blends almond milk into the liquid mixture, contradicting the ingredient note stating almond milk is optional to loosen the mixture. Blending liquid upfront with cottage cheese and maple syrup can make the final dough too wet depending on the protein powder brand.
